_comment: The situational variable vocabulary. Shared by naming.py (add-ins, servers) and
naming.js (the companion windows) — this file is the single source of truth for
both, exactly as theme.css is for the look.
A parameter name is CamelCase words. Any word that appears here is a VARIABLE: it
is stripped out to leave the STEM, and recorded as a tag. Names that differ only in
their variables therefore collapse into one family, and the situation at the moment
you are typing picks the member.
EdgeBackOffsetY   stem EdgeOffset   {direction: Back, axis: Y}
EdgeFrontOffsetY  stem EdgeOffset   {direction: Front, axis: Y}
EdgeOffsetX       stem EdgeOffset   {axis: X}
EdgeOffsetZ       stem EdgeOffset   {axis: Z}
Every word is matched as a WHOLE CamelCase word, so acronyms are safe: HIPSThickness
splits as HIPS + Thickness and never yields a bare axis letter.
axis   the world axis. 'end' is not meaningful; the axis word alone locates nothing,
which is exactly what makes it the right tag for a symmetric axis or for a
midline.
direction  an axis AND which end of it. 'high' is the positive end (Right +X, Back
+Y, Top +Z); 'low' is the negative end. Bounds values are positive OUTWARD, so
the world coordinate of a high bound is +value and of a low bound is -value,
and the span between them is (high + low).
span   the half-extent of a SYMMETRIC axis, measured midline to side. Offered only
where that axis is set symmetric on the component; on an asymmetric axis these
words are filtered out of the vocabulary entirely rather than given a second
meaning.
_relativeTypes: Measurement types whose value is measured FROM the direction named in the same
name, rather than from the origin. 'ShelfOffsetBack' is 30mm in from the BACK
bound; 'FrontPosition' merely locates the front in world space, which is
origin-framed like everything else. That distinction is a parameter's FRAME, and
it is what lets a dimension starting at the origin stop offering parameters
measured from a bound. Matched case-insensitively against the last word of the
stem. Extend this list if another word ever means the same thing.
